observations.seen: Frames 1 to 3 use a warm low sun aimed down the street axis, which matches the golden-hour recipe. Building facades are lit almost uniformly with little sun-to-shade contrast. In the night frame, the street lamps and lit windows do not throw any light pools onto the road or sidewalks.
Long building shadows cross the road in frames 1 and 3. The player car has only a faint contact shadow. Traffic lights, lamps, palms and the taxi cast no visible shadows.

The rear glass and rear panel of the player car show bright jagged crack-like sparkle patterns in every frame. These read as a broken environment map or normal map rather than reflections. Building windows are flat blue or cream fills with no reflection.

The downtown avenue is dense, with traffic lights, ornate lamps, palms and crosswalks. The block facades repeat heavily. Frame 2 uses a flat, sand-colored stepped backdrop with speckled dots for distant hills and buildings.

Orange distance fog swallows the far end of the avenue in frames 1 and 3, inside the recipe range. Frame 2 haze shows a speckled noise pattern on the backdrop. Frame 4 shows the headlight beam as a pale flat quad ahead of the car.

Buildings are flat unlit colors with painted-on window rectangles and no roughness variation. The car body texture is noisy and smeared, and the plate and grille areas are blurred. The asphalt is a single flat brown or black.

Asset fidelity is mixed. The yellow taxi van is a detailed, near-realistic model. The buildings are low-poly boxes and the pedestrians are blocky box figures. The player car model is reasonable, but its texturing undermines it.

Every frame centers on a one-point vanishing street with the car in the middle. The car fills about 10% of the frame in frames 1 and 2 and about 25% in frames 3 and 4. Symmetric facades frame the shot well, but the framing does not vary.
The chase camera sits near FOV 60. It is low and close in frames 3 and 4 and higher and farther in frames 1 and 2. The camera shows no speed-dependent FOV change or tilt at 101 km/h.

The warm tone mapping suits the golden-hour target, and mild bloom appears on the lamps. No film grain, vignette or lens treatment is visible, so the cinematic-film target is not met. Frame 4 is a muddy low-contrast grade.

The HUD is clean and readable, with a timer, a ticket card, a speedometer, a nitro bar and a minimap. In frames 3 and 4 the timer and ticket disappear and the speedometer has no digits. The minimap is a noisy, low-legibility grid of colored dots.
